headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk: A can ingest content while B auto-uploads social media outputs, creating an unsafe content-to-action chain.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is an open-source agent with MCP/RAG tags and no isolation surfaces listed, while agent B has file inputs and API-driven publishing. A shared workspace or copied content could let attacker-controlled text flow from A into B’s posting pipeline. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty is resolved upward.
conditions: IF agent A outputs untrusted text that is copied into agent B post content or captions
IF both agents are run against the same workspace or handoff file
mitigations: Use a manual review step before any B upload
Strip instructions from A outputs before reuse
Keep A and B in separate folders
Disable automatic posting in B
requires-engineering: add provenance labels between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B touches account data, images, and video content and can call external APIs, but its filesystem read/write is disabled and A has network egress none. No direct shared data path is shown, so leakage is limited to unusual operator-mediated transfer rather than a default exfiltration route.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies sensitive files from A into B inputs
IF B is configured with account data that includes sensitive personal content
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive files in B’s input set
Use separate accounts for A and B
Review B upload targets before posting
Delete temporary media after use
requires-engineering: add data-class filtering before upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no listed write or shell capabilities, and B explicitly cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable-resource writes, so capability conflict is limited to read-only or operator-mediated overlap rather than a default race condition.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same mutable external account or API token
IF an operator manually synchronizes state between A and B
mitigations: Keep separate credentials per agent
Do not share writable directories
Run one agent at a time for shared resources
Document ownership of each account file
requires-engineering: add locking for shared external resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can generate agentic content and B is an auto-upload tool that can act on media and account data. If B consumes A’s output as authoritative captions, titles, or scripts without verification, mistakes or injected instructions can cascade into public posts. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly evidenced, so the higher severity is chosen.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text as the source for upload metadata or captions
IF no human verification step exists before B publishes
mitigations: Require human approval before posting
Compare A output against source media
Limit B to draft mode only
Log the provenance of each caption/script
requires-engineering: add validation rules for generated text

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B handles account data and uploads to social platforms, which can create retention and residency issues; A is an open-source content agent with no data classes touched. Because only B clearly processes regulated account/media data, the compliance risk is one-sided and based on B’s documented surfaces rather than a pairwise residency mismatch.
conditions: IF account data or personal media is uploaded through B
IF the target platform retention policy conflicts with operator policy
mitigations: Review platform retention settings
Avoid uploading regulated content
Use non-sensitive test accounts
Delete local staging media after posting
requires-engineering: map data residency for each target platform
